name: AD743 / AD745
tagline: ADI BiFET single with 2.9 nV/√Hz and only 6.9 fA/√Hz: a reference choice for MM phono, piezo and hydrophones.

lineage.note: Models credited 'AAG / PMI' and 'ARG / PMI' (1992), 'ARG / ADSC' (1995). Reportedly designed by Scott Wurcer.

key_specs.value: 2.9 nV/√Hz typ (at 10 kHz); 0.38 µV p-p 0.1–10 Hz
key_specs.source: AD743 Rev. E, AD745 Rev. D; Rubiola

key_specs.value: 9.6 V to 30 V total (±4.8 V to ±15 V)
p-channel JFET pair, bipolar gain and output stages

reputation.summary: More an instrumentation legend than a rolling favourite. 2.9 nV/√Hz voltage noise with only 6.9 fA/√Hz current noise keeps it quiet with low and very high source impedances, so it suits hydrophone, piezo and charge amplifiers; Rubiola chose the AD743 for AM-noise detectors. A niche MM phono following is reported, unconfirmed. No community listening reports found.
typical_uses: MM phono / RIAA input stage (reported niche following)
Hydrophone and piezo-film charge amps (AD745 with PVDF film)
Low-noise measurement front ends (Rubiola AM/phase-noise detectors)
Cryogenic bolometer readout and precision bias (arXiv physics/9902042)
caveats: Single only, in 16-lead SOIC (R-16) or DIP: dual DIP-8 sockets need two parts and an adapter.
AD745 is compensated for higher gains (minimum believed 5); not a unity-gain buffer.
20 pF input capacitance (model) forms a pole with large feedback resistors; add a feedback capacitor.
~8 mA per amplifier and at least ±4.8 V supply; not a 5 V single-supply part.
Several R-16 reel and leaded variants discontinued via ADI PDNs; check which orderables remain.

counterfeit_notes: No AD743/AD745 fake reports found. Checks: ~8 mA supply current at ±15 V (a remarked TL071 draws far less and is noisier); SMD should be R-16, not SOIC-8; 'new' leaded AD745KR-16 is old stock at best. Buy from authorised channels.
alternatives: Discrete LSK170/LSK489 JFET front end plus op-amp
